text:
Cole Perfetti spent his early career as a useful middle-six piece in Winnipeg. This season the Jets have handed him 18:14 a night, up from 15:37, and a spot on the ice for 90% of their power-play chances, after half of them last year. He's answered with 19 points in 22 games, nearly double last season's rate.

It isn't luck. His own chances are up to 1.43 expected goals per 60 from 1.08, he has eight goals on 9.6 expected, and he's fired 61 shots. By wins added from his goals he ranks 29th of 542 skaters, and he scored the power-play goal that started the comeback in Chicago on Saturday. Winnipeg won six straight in his last ten games before a 2-1 loss in Ottawa.

The interesting twist is where his value came from last season. Evolving-Hockey had most of it at the defensive end, 95th percentile among forwards at suppressing chances. If that part of his game holds while the offense grows, the Jets have a player who's more than a power-play passenger. BVM Sports asked whether he's starting to drive his own line. Our numbers say yes.
headline: Perfetti is driving his own line now
